standard_prerequisites: The definition of a prime divisor on an integral good algebraic space and of the associated Weil divisor, and the identification of codimension one points with the local rings of dimension one
The definition of a dimension function and its compatibility with codimension, so that codimension one means delta-dimension one less
The local description of an effective Cartier divisor as the zero scheme of a nonzerodivisor on an etale neighbourhood, and Krull's principal ideal theorem
core_obligations: Part one: combine the definition of a prime divisor, the identification of codimension one points through the local rings, and the definition of a dimension function to obtain the equivalence of the three conditions
Part two: for an irreducible component of an effective Cartier divisor choose its generic point and an etale neighbourhood on which the divisor is cut out by a nonzerodivisor

Note that the chosen point is a generic point of the zero scheme of that nonzerodivisor, apply the principal ideal theorem to conclude that its local ring has dimension one, and read off that the point is a codimension one point, hence the component is a prime divisor and its delta-dimension is one less
proof_roadmap: Get the equivalence of the three characterisations of a prime divisor from the definitions
Reduce the statement about components of effective Cartier divisors to a local computation on an etale neighbourhood
Apply the principal ideal theorem and the codimension one characterisation
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the characterisation of prime divisors and of components of effective Cartier divisors by their delta-dimension at source lines 1592-1607, label lemma-divisor-delta-dimension, whose proof occupies source lines 1609-1630. Part one is a pure unpacking of three definitions, but part two requires a local argument: the irreducible component is replaced by its generic point, an etale neighbourhood is chosen on which the effective Cartier divisor is cut out by a nonzerodivisor, the point is recognised as a generic point of the zero scheme of that nonzerodivisor, and the principal ideal theorem is invoked to conclude that the local ring there has dimension one. Only then does the codimension one characterisation give the statement. The counted statement records neither the neighbourhood nor the appeal to the principal ideal theorem.
